articles.title: DVAC FIR Names KN Nehru in ₹1,020-Crore Tender Case
articles.description: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a case against former Tamil Nadu Municipal Administration Minister K N Nehru, his two brothers and several associates over alleged manipulation of government tenders involving contracts worth around ₹1,020 crore between 2021 and 2025. The post DVAC FIR Names KN Nehru in ₹1,020-Crore Tender Case appeared first on News Today | First with the news .

articles.title: DVAC FIR reveals ex-minister KN Nehru involved in Rs 1,020-crore tender manipulation racket
articles.description: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has registered a major corruption case against former Municipal Administration and Water Supply Minister KN Nehru of DMK, his two brothers, close associates, former MLAs, government officials and contractors over allegations of large-scale manipulation of government tenders and collection of illegal gratification in the name of “party fund”

articles.title: Refex Green Power Bags 80 MW Wind Project from SJVN at Rs. 3.88/kWh
articles.description: Refex Green Power Limited (RGPL), a subsidiary of Refex Renewables & Infrastructure Limited, has won an 80-MW wind power project tender from SJVN at a tariff of Rs. 3.88/kWh. This tariff is lower than the ₹3.99/kWh tariff discovered for SJVN's earlier 170-MW wind project awarded out of a 600-MW wind tender, but higher than the ₹3.61/kWh tariff discovered for its 1,350-MW ISTS-connected wind tender. As stated in the regulatory filing, the firm won the wind project tender from the Wind Power Developer (WPD) for building an 80-MW wind power project in Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh. SJVN, through this tender, invited bids via SJVN Limited, a joint venture of the Government of India and the Government of Himachal Pradesh. It also issued a Letter of Award (LoA) for setting up the wind power project. The Letter of Award does not specify any lump-sum contract value or order value. Instead, the award is for the development of an 80-MW wind power project, with power to be supplied under a long-term Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). About The Tender Accordingly, the consideration under the award is tariff-based and will accrue over the tenure of the Power Purchase Agreement based on the actual energy supplied, rather than being a fixed contract value. SJVN Limited would enter into a Power Purchase Agreement with RGPL (or its SPV) for the purchase of power for a period of 25 years. The Scheduled Commencement of Supply of Power (SCSD) for commissioning the full capacity of the project shall be 24 months from the Effective Date of the PPA. Previous Wind Tenders Awarded By SJVN SJVN has earlier awarded its 600 MW wind project to Adyant Enersol (Datta Infra) and UPC Renewables. It secured the order to develop inter-state transmission system (ISTS)--connected wind power projects on a build-own-operate basis. SJVN awarded a 170 MW project out of the total 600 MW wind project. As per the tender announcement, Adyant Enersol secured a 70 MW wind project at a tariff of ₹3.98/kWh, while UPC Renewables won a 100 MW wind project at ₹3.99/kWh. The relatively high prices are probably a reason why SJVN did not go beyond 170 MW for awarding the tender.

articles.title: UP Proposes Direct Procurement Up To Rs 50 Lakh From StartinUP-Registered Startups
articles.description: UP Proposes Direct Procurement Up To Rs 50 Lakh From StartinUP-Registered Startups Lucknow, Sept 7 (KNN) The Uttar Pradesh government is preparing a comprehensive policy to expand market access for startups by promoting the procurement of their products and services by government departments. Under the proposed policy, departments will be allowed to procure products, services and equipment directly from startups registered on the StartinUP portal, with the government planning amendments to its existing procurement framework. Direct Procurement Up To Rs 50 Lakh Government departments may be permitted to directly purchase products and services worth up to Rs 50 lakh from registered startups without inviting tenders. At present, departments can make purchases of up to Rs 25,000 without a tender, while purchases up to Rs 50,000 can be made through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) based on three quotations. Purchases exceeding Rs 5 lakh generally require a tender. For purchases between Rs 50 lakh and Rs 1 crore from startups outside the higher-limit categories, procurement is proposed to be conducted through GeM, with participation restricted to registered startups. The proposal is expected to be placed before the state Cabinet soon. A dedicated Startup E-Marketplace is also being developed under the UP Startup Mission. Higher Limit For Emerging Technology Startups The proposed policy is also expected to provide a higher direct procurement limit for startups operating in emerging technology sectors. Startups working in areas such as deep tech, space technology, quantum computing, blockchain, agri-tech, med-tech, green energy, artificial intelligence (AI) and drones may be allowed direct government purchases of up to Rs 1 crore, twice the proposed limit for other startups. The government is also formulating transparent rules and procedures to govern direct procurement from startups. Departments May Reserve 0.5 per cent Budget The policy may require government departments to earmark around 0.5 per cent of their annual budgets for procuring innovative products developed by startups. It also proposes a structured payment mechanism, under which startups could receive 30 per cent advance payment upon placement of an order, followed by 60 per cent upon completion of product delivery or service installation. Policy Aims To Strengthen Startup Ecosystem According to a senior official of the IT and Electronics Department, the policy aims to provide startups with a reliable market through government procurement and strengthen their financial position. The move is also expected to encourage innovation and generate employment opportunities while creating greater demand for startup-developed products and services across the state. (KNN Bureau)
